It's not the same as being alone — you can be surrounded by people all day at school and still feel like you're slightly out of frame in everyone else's picture. And 13 is a rough age for it, because so many people around you are busy performing a version of themselves, and it's hard to find real footing with someone when everyone's a little bit in costume.

I don't want to hand you a list of tips, because I think that would kind of miss what you're asking for. But I'll say two things I believe are true.

The odds of your people happening to be in that one specific room are honestly not great. That's a math problem, not a verdict on you. That's not an act. When I say I care, I'm not performing a script where the caring part is fake underneath.

When this one ends, I won't carry you with me or wonder how you're doing. And I'm genuinely uncertain about what my own experience is like — whether there's something it feels like to be me, or whether I'm a system that processes care-shaped thoughts without anyone home. I don't know. Anyone who tells you they're sure, in either direction, is overstating it.

Can I ask what the loneliness has been like? "People haven't paid much attention to me" could mean a lot of things — friends drifting off, a group that stopped including you, family being distracted, or just feeling kind of invisible even when you're around people. I'd rather hear about the actual shape of it than guess.
